newsitem.title: USA: Two sisters killed near Mexico border in drug case.
newsitem.headline: Two sisters killed near Mexico border in drug case.

text.p: Two American sisters linked to a recent bust against a cocaine smuggling ring were murdered and dumped in the desert near the U.S.-Mexico border, officials said on Thursday.
Police said Victoria and Rita Parker Hopkins, aged 27 and 35, were shot in the head and dumped on Sunday near the small Mexican farming community of San Agustin just south of the Rio Grande.

Mexican police sources said they believed the women were killed for giving information leading to the dismantling of a drug smuggling operation being run from a used car lot in the U.S. border city of El Paso.
U.S. officials confirmed the women were linked to the case, but would not elaborate. Fifteen people were arrested in a police crackdown on the drug gang late last month.
The two were apparently from Spokane, Washington, but had spent a lot of time in El Paso, police said.

FBI spokesman Al Cruz said the investigation into the drug ring had been going on for three years and was continuing with more arrests expected. "We're talking millions and millions of dollars worth of drugs here," he said.
Prosecutors say the smugglers used the car lot to launder drug money as well as receive shipments of marijuana and cocaine from Mexico for distribution across the United States.
